rationale:
Evidence from iteration 3 (score 405, up from 198): the change to forward sensors at y=0.08, a wider spread, wheel_track 0.10, mass 0.6 and kd 1.0 roughly doubled the score. Oval finish rate is 55% and s-bend is 25%. Slalom still fails on every trial (0 finishes, progress 0.20). Every failure is off_track at max_error about 0.06 m, the binding limit, since max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 for any allowed body width. Steering oscillation is 0.18 to 0.28, which means the loop still overshoots at bends. Mean oval finish time is 1.93 s, so the robot has speed margin under the 3 s limit.

Changes in this candidate, kept to two levers so the effect can be read: (1) kd 1.0 to 1.5, to damp the oscillation that is still present on the bends and the tight slalom. (2) mass 0.6 to 0.5 kg, lowering yaw inertia so the robot changes heading faster when the line curves sharply. Geometry is otherwise unchanged: sensors stay at y=0.08 with the same spread, wheel_track 0.10, base_speed 1.0, kp 5.5, ki 0 and line_loss last_direction. Speed is not raised, because off-track exits are the failure mode and a faster robot would reach the bends with less correction time.

Expected result: steering_oscillation falls below about 0.22, slalom progress rises above 0.25, and s-bend finishes increase. Oval completion should hold. Hypotheses: H1, kd is the limit on the bends, shown by steering_oscillation dropping and max_error staying below 0.06 on more seeds. H2, lower mass speeds up turning, shown by slalom progress rising at the same base_speed. H3, if slalom still leaves the line at its first sharp direction change, the next lever is wider sensor coverage or a larger sensor_size, not more gain. Next measurements: progress and completion_time for speed versus stability, max_error and line_loss_events for stability, steering_oscillation for damping, control_effort for gain cost, and noise_robustness to check margin against the held-back tracks.
